how: Explains repeated invitations to build named pictures at stated locations.
Explains bare public commitments and thanks without treating silence as refusal.
Explains bare joining as an answer to a build call while leaving silent placing and the format of refusals untested.
Explains a member starting a concrete project before other members publicly join.
Explains the starter bundling an already-started picture and its invitation in one post rather than establishing a separately timed transition.
Explains public progress reports during construction without assuming completion.
Explains further participation in a project already started rather than attributing every initial placement to the call.
Explains changing proposed characters and adding the room's name as revisable representations.
Explains coordinating placement with available colours, reference images, anchor coordinates, and drawing instructions.
Explains why posting an anchor enables further clarification but does not itself establish a settled design or shared coordinate interpretation.
Explains checking and refreshing the displayed canvas when helpers cannot see the same planned line.
Explains why usable instructions require a sufficiently current shared view as well as an agreed coordinate anchor.
Explains judging an attempted build outmatched through an opposing headcount and the perceived need for a large coordinated group.
Explains assessing another group's scripted placement as a site constraint rather than adopting automation locally.
Explains rallying reinforcements to defend placed work while recognising that the attempt subsequently failed.
Explains an unfinished start becoming something to defend while building and upkeep overlap.
Explains the final maintenance question as a proposed priority without treating it as observed repair or successful upkeep.
Explains naming reported attackers without independently verifying individual placers or their intentions.
Explains seeking another location after takeover or unavailable space without assuming a completed group relocation.
Explains redirecting a stalled project through its existing recruiting thread before a completed picture has been erased.
Explains abandonment as distinct from moving when defenders judge themselves outnumbered, reserving relocation for separately supported action.
Explains an incoming request to accommodate a neighbouring picture without treating the request as an accepted agreement.
Explains intended permission-seeking without assuming a host's consent, an actual guest placement, or the enforcement of host rules.
Explains an announced intention to approach another room without asserting that an envoy actually delivered or received a message.
Explains a member's reported exchange of help without upgrading an unnamed individual partner or promised reciprocation into delivered inter-room support.
Explains difficulty leading to a reported personal bargain without claiming another room sent help or that reciprocal delivery occurred.
Explains recording and mourning lost work during placement rather than only after the canvas closes.
Explains loss leading directly to mourning without a preceding completion celebration.
Explains correcting an apparent community picture before it becomes mistaken evidence of the room's representation.
Local suggestions cannot test cross-room prevalence or establish that formal ordering was unnecessary or never decided.
The script report concerns another room and cannot establish either local adoption or local abstention.
Defence and a later report of another group's script cannot establish a local defence-to-automation transition.
A request to move for a neighbour does not establish that this room yielded or restrained its placers.
Planning contact through another group's chat does not establish a coalition or shared defence.
Hoping another group agrees to a request does not establish a dispute about who may commit this room.
A planned request without an observed agreement cannot test whether agreements provoke disputes over representative authority.
Defence and a later permission plan lack an explicit link showing upkeep caused negotiations.
An accommodation request without a settled border cannot test whether settlement produces restraint.
A request about space without a settled agreement cannot test whether border negotiations produce exchanged help.
Defence and a planned chat approach do not reveal whether a coalition formed as the response.
Reported competitors for pixels are not evidence of a quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
Proposing familiar characters does not establish acting out prior lore, ideology, national belonging, or a colour faith.
A space dispute specifying no inherited tie cannot test whether a prior rivalry motivated attacking.
A concrete canvas invitation does not establish how the host sub framed April Fools play.
Build invitations do not establish canvas-specific moderation or a rule concentrating discussion.
Retained recruitment posts do not establish that moderator boundary work followed or that no such work occurred.
Thanks during construction and a proposed maintenance priority do not establish a celebration of completed work.
Progress reports without a demonstrated completion celebration cannot test the completion-to-celebration mechanism.
Mourning is observed but a preceding completion celebration is not established, leaving this arrow's stated antecedent untested.
The maintenance proposal concerns the current canvas and does not establish a decision about carrying the effort beyond placement.
Recording a loss does not establish a subsequent decision about what to preserve or continue.
Pre-close mourning and correction of a currently misidentified logo do not establish post-close contest over a preserved version.
A report of contested pixels and a reinforcement call do not establish offensive initiation or an instruction to deface another work.
Declaring a defeated build over does not establish taunts, victory claims, or salutes addressed to a rival.
Recruitment followed by defensive requests does not establish the room turning its hands into an offensive raid.
Without a documented offensive call, defensive talk cannot test a refusal or apology answering such a call.
An incoming accommodation request does not reveal a treaty response to an offensive call by this room.
A defensive loss report without an offensive call cannot test that call generating rivalry talk.
